name: Christopher Olah
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026)
forbes_bio: Chris Olah is cofounder and interpretability research lead at Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems.
He cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other ex-OpenAI employees.
Anthropic, which private investors valued at $380 billion in February 2026, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon.
Olah previously worked in a similar role at OpenAI and was a researcher at Google Brain.
Olah skipped college and was named a Thiel Fellow in 2012, when he was 19. In 2020, he wrote a blog post to help others decide if they should follow a similar path.

name: Liu Jincheng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2010-2026)
forbes_bio: Liu Jincheng is the chairman of Eve Energy, a battery maker listed in China's tech hub Shenzhen.
A smaller competitor to China's BYD and CATL, Eve Energy supplies to auto, wearable devices, renewable energy and other sectors.
Born in a village in China's central Hubei province, Liu worked at a state-owned factory upon graduating college.
He later went on to study electrochemistry at Wuhan University, and worked as a battery engineer before founding Eve Energy in 2000.
Eve Energy ranked second globally in energy storage battery shipment in 2025.

name: Martin Viessmann
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2005-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Martin Viessmann is chairman of the executive board of Viessmann Generations Group, a family-owned investment company with the self-stated goal of "co-creating living spaces for future generations."
He is the grandson of founder Johann Viessmann. The private company has 12,000 employees and 23 production divisions in 12 countries.
Martin envisions a world where CO2 emissions are reduced by 80% and the consumption of fossil energy by two-thirds.
In 2012, the firm received the Energy Globe Award for Sustainability in the "Air" category. In 2013, Martin was named Greentech Manager of the Year.
Martin's son, Maximilian, is the company's co-CEO. His daughter, Anna Katharina, is a non-executive member of the board of the family holding company.
forbes_facts: Viessmann Group is a prominent sponsor of winter sports and underwrites the Viessmann Academy, which provides training for heating architects and engineers.
A fitness buff and passionate skier, Martin holds an honorary doctorate from the University of Wisconsin and has a professional pilot's license.
